  "question": "What has been proposed to reduce the risk of a reinforcement-learning agent becoming substantially worse after updates based on unreliable estimates from limited experience, and by what mechanism?",
  "reference_answer": "Rerouted Behavior Improvement (RBI) proposes restricting policy updates with a reroute constraint. For each action and state, the new probability is the old behavior-policy probability multiplied by a factor bounded between c_min and c_max. The reasoning is that rarely sampled actions have less reliable value estimates, so allowing large probability increases for those actions can turn an apparently beneficial update into a damaging one. Under the simplified independent-sample analysis, the variance associated with the potential performance loss depends on the squared probability change divided by the old action probability. Bounding the multiplicative change controls this term, limiting how strongly estimation errors can affect the updated policy and bounding the variance of the improvement penalty. RBI can then seek better estimated performance within these restrictions by solving a linear program. This is a proposed safeguard against damaging updates, not an unconditional guarantee that every update improves performance.",

    "has a higher error for actions that were taken less frequently, thus, to avoid improvement penalty, we must restrict the ratio of the change in probability",
    "\\pi(a|s)=c(s,a)\\beta(a|s)",

    "\\frac{|\\beta(a|s)-\\pi(a|s)|^{2}}{\\beta(a|s)}",
    "and even a single mistake along the trajectory, caused by an unregulated element, might wreck the performance of the entire policy. However, by using the reroute constraint which tame each of these terms we can bound the variance of the improvement penalty.",
